audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital expenditure may be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest filed annual-capex expectation of $120–$130 million, previously $120–$140 million, versus FY2025 capex of $114.501 million and $74.4 million anchor OE; required adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any maintenance-capex shortfall is deducted directly from recurring OE and reduces every projected year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company currently expects that its net annual capital expenditures will be in the range of approximately $120 to $140 million going forward in order to maintain a modern store base.
audit_findings.explanation: Understatement is not demonstrated because the maintenance charge embedded in OE was not supplied and the guidance includes reopening and potentially growth spending. However, the filed annual range is larger than the entire OE anchor and is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion if the model deducted materially less recurring maintenance.
audit_findings.action: Reproduce FY2025 OE line by line and reconcile its maintenance-capex deduction to the latest $120–$130 million guidance, separately identifying reopening, new-store, land, expansion, reconstruction, and insured expenditures; rerun all scenarios with the supported maintenance amount.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may classify operating cash as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $455.086566 million added to equity, equal to $23.96 per diluted share and 30.3% of the $1.500 billion base equity value; required reserve unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash dollar-for-dollar to common-equity value; any working-capital, self-insurance, capital-program, or other operating reserve must be excluded from surplus cash.
audit_findings.evidence: In general, the Company finances its capital expenditures to the extent possible from cash on hand and cash flow from operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The full cash addition is demonstrated, but the amount required in operations is unresolved. Because the cash addition represents nearly one-third of base equity value and the company funds capital expenditures partly from cash on hand, even a partial reclassification could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 cash balance to restricted, pledged, committed, self-insurance, working-capital, reconstruction, tax, and near-term capital needs; establish normalized minimum liquidity and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor and null perimeter ignore known temporary store closures
audit_findings.magnitude: $111.217 million of FY2025 retail sales attributed to temporarily closed stores, equal to 2.1% of FY2025 net sales; OE and rebuilding effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalizing lost store contribution would increase anchor OE, while reopening costs, incremental maintenance, and timing delays could reduce OE or the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Four stores sustained damage that required that they be temporarily closed, of which, as of the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, three remain closed and are currently expected to reopen at various times during 2026 or in 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The impaired FY2025 operating perimeter and continued closure of three stores through June 2026 are demonstrated. The record does not provide store-level margins, reopening capital, insurance offsets, or precise reopening dates, so it cannot establish the net value effect or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain store-level pre-storm sales and contribution, reopening schedules, remaining repair capital, and insurance recoveries; model the discrete recovery and costs or normalize the anchor and perimeter consistently.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 contains asymmetric hurricane costs and insurance recoveries
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.0 million of FY2025 cleanup and repair costs and $6.2 million of FY2025 insurance proceeds, a net $2.8 million pre-tax expense; OE normalization unverified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing nonrecurring costs raises OE, while removing insurance proceeds lowers OE; asymmetric treatment changes the anchor and all forecast and terminal values.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, for the year ended September 27, 2025, the Company incurred approximately $9.0 million in cleanup and repair costs and received aggregate insurance proceeds of $6.2 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring amounts are demonstrated, but their treatment in the $74.4 million anchor is not. Each gross amount is large relative to the anchor, and asymmetric normalization is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion even though the reported net expense is smaller.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $9.0 million costs, $4.7 million inventory proceeds, and $1.5 million property proceeds through the OE calculation and related taxes; remove all nonrecurring storm effects symmetrically without removing ordinary maintenance, then rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Positive growth assumes transaction erosion is temporary
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 transactions excluding fuel declined 4.2%; valuation assumes 3% base and 5% bull growth, with computed values of $78.99 and $85.42 per share versus $70.56 at 0% growth
audit_findings.mechanism: Persistent traffic or real-volume contraction would reduce projected OE growth and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of transactions (excluding fuel) decreased 4.2% while the average transaction size (excluding fuel) increased by 0.1%.
audit_findings.explanation: The historical transaction decline is demonstrated, but whether it persists is forward-looking. Subsequent evidence is mixed: nine-month fiscal 2026 grocery comparable sales excluding fuel increased 0.4%, while the June 2026 quarter declined 3.1%. The risk should therefore be monitored rather than treated as a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Track post-reopening transactions, units, price and mix, comparable-store sales, margins, and store productivity; rerun growth assumptions if sustained traffic and real-volume data fail to support positive OE growth.

audit_findings.title: A nonqualified-plan claim may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 liability of $32.459 million less corresponding plan assets of $29.881 million equals a $2.578 million deficit, or $0.14 per diluted share and 0.17% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Only the plan deficit, after matching restricted trust assets to the participant liability, would be deducted from the common-equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The liability to plan participants totaled $ 32.5 million at September 27, 2025 and $ 28.9 million at September 28, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The alleged bridge omission is not demonstrated, but the filed FY2025 net deficit provides a concrete upper-scale comparison. A $2.578 million deduction would reduce the $78.99 base value by approximately $0.14 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. June 2026 plan assets increased to $32.749 million, although the corresponding liability was not separately disclosed.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 plan liability, match it exclusively to the $32.749 million restricted plan assets, confirm neither side is already included elsewhere in the bridge, and deduct any current residual deficit once.
